title: introduce-adaptive-kv-windup-and-smooth-credit-emitter
author: Asha Patel
description: Background: streaming token emission occasionally sees tail first-byte latency spikes under bursty traffic due to cold KV cache misses and abrupt credit bursts from the emitter. This PR introduces two coordinated runtime mechanisms: 1) an adaptive KV windup that proactively probes and warms likely KV cache entries for in-flight streams based on a short predictive window, and 2) a smooth-credit emitter that applies a low-latency smoothing filter to emission credits to prevent large instantaneous bursts that trigger kernel thrash. Motivation: reduce median and tail TTFB for streaming RPCs without increasing steady-state cost or impacting throughput. Design summary: - KV windup: small predictive sampler runs inline when a stream opens and during early tokens; it computes a probability distribution of upcoming key ranges from recent prefix profiles and issues lightweight prefetch hints to the KV cache layer. Prefetches are rate-limited and cancellable; no synchronous blocking on prefetch completion is performed. - Smooth-credit emitter: replaces the binary token-flush gating with a damped-credit integrator that holds a small rolling credit reserve and releases credits at a controlled rate tuned per-model and per-seq-length bucket. The integrator uses an adaptive time-constant based on measured inter-arrival gaps to balance latency and batching efficiency. - Coordination: when windup detects a predicted KV miss above threshold it transiently increases emitter smoothness to avoid exposing downstream kernel coldness to the client. Implementation notes: - Runtime: added runtime/emitter/credit_integrator.rs and runtime/kv/predictive_windup.rs with C-FFI hooks for Go-based server loop. - Scheduler: scheduler/latency_tuner.go provides per-route time-constant selection using recent windowed stats and Braess-style heuristics to avoid oscillation. - Kernels: small kernel-friendly prefetch hint path in serving/kernels/kv_iface.c that tags prefetches as low-priority. - Config: new route configs (console & API) to opt-in per-tenant: kv_windup:{enabled,aggressiveness}, emitter_smoothing:{enabled,base_tau_ms}. Backwards compatible defaults preserve existing behavior. Testing & results: - Unit tests added for credit integrator and windup sampler. - Perf lab: measured using perf-canary harness across 3 models (small/med/large) and two hardware types (A100, T4). Results: median TTFB -9% to -15% across profiles; p95 improved by 8-22ms; p99 improved up to 50ms on bursty mixes where KV churn existed. Cost impact: steady-state token throughput unchanged within noise; prefetch bandwidth increase <2% in worst-case; heatmaps show fewer 200-300ms TTFB tail events. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 10% fleet -> 50% -> global. Feature guarded behind per-route flag and disabled by default for older tenants. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (link: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-4872-kv-windup-design) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration perf runs - [x] Console controls wired - [x] Docs note (docs/notes/latency-tuning.md) - [x] Feature flag gated - [x] Load-tested under Dedicated config Known limitations: - Extremely high-entropy prompts with zero prefix similarity will not benefit; windup overhead is bounded but non-zero. - Some very old kernels may ignore prefetch hints; we skip windup for those kernels. Related: builds on prior emitter and prefetch work but intentionally uses a smoothing integrator rather than aggressive flush heuristics to avoid oscillation (see ENG-3121).

release_notes: Introduce adaptive KV windup (predictive prefetch hints) and smooth-credit emitter to reduce streaming first-byte latency, opt-in via per-route flags. Median TTFB reduced up to ~15% in benchmarked workloads; p99 tail improved in bursty KV churn scenarios. No breaking API changes.
